Adipose: Loose connective tissue made of adipocytes that stores energy as triglyceride, insulates, cushions organs and acts as an endocrine organ (leptin, adiponectin); this model is abdominal subcutaneous fat.
Brain: The part of the central nervous system inside the skull - cerebrum, diencephalon, brainstem and cerebellum - that integrates sensory input, controls movement and autonomic function, and supports cognition.
Left eye: The paired sensory organ of vision in the orbit; the cornea and lens focus light on the retina, whose photoreceptors send signals through the optic nerve.
Right eye: The paired sensory organ of vision in the orbit; the cornea and lens focus light on the retina, whose photoreceptors send signals through the optic nerve.
Left knee: The synovial joint between the femur, tibia and patella, stabilised by the cruciate and collateral ligaments and cushioned by the medial and lateral menisci.
Right knee: The synovial joint between the femur, tibia and patella, stabilised by the cruciate and collateral ligaments and cushioned by the medial and lateral menisci.
Large intestine: The final part of the digestive tract (caecum, appendix, colon, rectum and anal canal) that absorbs water and electrolytes and stores faeces.
Lung: The paired respiratory organ in the thoracic cavity in which inhaled air in the alveoli exchanges oxygen and carbon dioxide with pulmonary capillary blood.
Lymph node: Small encapsulated secondary lymphoid organ along lymphatic vessels that filters lymph; B cells in follicles and T cells in the paracortex meet antigen here.
Mouth: The oral cavity at the start of the digestive tract, bounded by the lips, cheeks, palate and floor of the mouth, containing the teeth and tongue.
Pelvis: The bony ring formed by the two hip bones (ilium, ischium and pubis) and the sacrum and coccyx, which transmits body weight to the lower limbs and protects the pelvic organs.
Prostate: Walnut-sized male accessory gland below the bladder that surrounds the prostatic urethra and secretes an alkaline fluid (with PSA) forming part of the semen.
Sternum: The flat midline bone of the anterior chest wall (manubrium, body and xiphoid process) that articulates with the clavicles and costal cartilages.
Intervertebral disk: Fibrocartilaginous pad between adjacent vertebral bodies with an outer annulus fibrosus and an inner gel-like nucleus pulposus that absorbs load.
Trachea: The cartilaginous airway (C-shaped rings) from the larynx at C6 to its bifurcation into the main bronchi at about T4-T5 (carina).
Left palatine tonsil: Lymphoid tissue in the tonsillar fossa between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches, part of Waldeyer's ring.
Right palatine tonsil: Lymphoid tissue in the tonsillar fossa between the palatoglossal and palatopharyngeal arches, part of Waldeyer's ring.
Lymph node: Small encapsulated secondary lymphoid organ along lymphatic vessels that filters lymph; B cells in follicles and T cells in the paracortex meet antigen here.
